newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT - Brazil's CRT started as a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Brazil's CRT started as a buy.

text.p: ING Barings said it has initiated coverage of Rio Grande do Sul state's Cia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes, known commonly as CRT, with a buy recommendation.
-- ING analyst Patrick Jurczak also said in a report that the Dutch investment bank set a June 1998 price target for CRT of $211 per 100 shares.
-- "We assume that CRT should be trading at least at a 10-percent premium to the Latin (American) average," he wrote.
-- CRT, which trades on the SOMA over-the-counter market in Rio de Janeiro, expects to list on the Sao Paulo bourse in within the next two months, he added. Its ticker symbol is 1CRTAN.
-- Jurczak said the firm's projected line growth is superior to that of federal giant Telebras' operating subsidiaries.
-- "The number of lines will increase 35 percent year-on-year in 1997 and 27 percent year-on-year in 1998, accumulating a two-year's growth of 71 percent," he said.

-- He also cited Telefonica de Espana's management of the firm, earnings growth higher than the Latin American average, its marketing strategy and a retirement plan that cut CRT's workforce by 25 percent last year.
-- Jurczak said he took into account a projected 41-percent decrease in monthly cellular rental fees and a 25-percent decline in cellular installation fees in 1998 due to the opening of competition.
-- His forecasts also include the transfer of 10 percent of long-distance revenues to Telebras long-distance unit Embratel in 1997 and 49 percent in 1998.
-- He said he set a June 1998 price target of $211 per 100 shares, "indicating a potential total return of 40 percent."
-- CRT's preferred A share closed Friday at 163.00 reais, off 0.58 percent from the prior session.
